messages:
Maya (CS): Kickoff: Lodestar week1 private/VPC onboarding. Main asks: 365d audit retention, quarterly KMS rotation proof (they asked for HSM-backed CMK), and signed export for their SOC team. Who's got blockers?
Tom (CSE): Preflight shows CIDR 10.30.0.0/22 allocated. Lodestar requested an additional /28 for bastion management. Need confirmation of NAT egress behavior and whether Splunk (collector.splunk.redwood.net:5514) will be reached via peering or a proxy.
Ivy (SRE): We created the VPC and a peering connection pcx-0f1e2d; route table RTB-lodestar-1 applied on our side. Waiting on Lodestar to accept peering and add reciprocal route. Requested their route table ID and acceptance token. Also provisioned NAT gw ngw-lst-02.
Arjun (Security): KMS plan: customer-managed HSM-backed CMK in Lodestar account with an explicit grant pattern from Redwood. I'll provide a minimal key policy and sample grant workflow. For rotation evidence we'll export CloudTrail events filtered on kms:RevokeGrant|kms:DisableKeyRotation|kms:EnableKeyRotation and produce a signed PDF.
Maya (CS): @Arjun please paste the key policy snippet so I can pass to Lodestar SecOps.
Arjun (Security): Example key policy (replace ARNs/IDs):
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRedwoodUsage",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDWOOD:role/redeem-infra"},
      "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:CreateGrant","kms:ListGrants","kms:DescribeKey"],
      "Resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "AllowAccountAdmins",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::LODESTAR:root"},
      "Action": "kms:*",
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```
Also recommend enabling automatic rotation and CloudTrail logging to an encrypted S3 bucket with 365d lifecycle.
InfraBot: Route apply RTB-lodestar-1 -> subnet-app-01 succeeded; NAT gateway ngw-lst-02 created (us-east-1a) :white_check_mark:
Tom (CSE): IAM cross-account role: Lodestar should create role RedwoodProvisioner with an AssumeRole policy for arn:aws:iam::REDWOOD:role/deploy-bot and scoped permissions: sts:AssumeRole, s3:PutObject to s3://lodestar-logs/redwood/, and kms:Encrypt for key ARN. I'll test once they share the role ARN.
Sam (Account Exec): Renewal flagged in 68 days. Lodestar is evaluating increased committed capacity if we can demonstrate audit & rotation artifacts within 5 business days of cutover. Delay here is a renewal risk.
Lodestar (Customer): We'll try to accept peering today and share route table id + role ARN. For the rotation proof: can you include a short statement we can upload to our compliance portal? Also prefer signed PDF.
Arjun (Security): Yes - we'll include a brief signed attestation, the CloudTrail extract, and a generated PDF. We'll drop it in the encrypted S3 bucket and give a presigned URL valid for 21 days.
Ivy (SRE): Peering status: accepted on our side; showing pcx-0f1e2d active. Still waiting on Lodestar acceptance event in their account. Sent CLI snippet to run: `aws ec2 accept-vpc-peering-connection --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0f1e2d --profile lodestar`.
Tom (CSE): Once Lodestar shares role ARN I'll do an assume-role + s3 put to `s3://lodestar-logs/redwood/test/` and return logs. Plan to run `aws sts assume-role` then `aws s3 cp --acl bucket-owner-full-control testfile`.
Maya (CS): Action list: 1) @Ivy confirm final peering acceptance 2) @Arjun finalize key policy + rotation export template + signed attestation 3) @Tom validate assume-role and test prefix 4) @Sam track renewal cadence with Legal/Finance. I'll consolidate and send to Lodestar.
InfraBot: Dry-run deployment started 2024-06-10T09:05:00Z step 2/5 succeeded (config applied); peering-state:pending
Maya (CS): We'll check back EOD PT. If peering not accepted, escalate to TAM and schedule an admin-to-admin call. Closing thread once we have route table id + role ARN + presigned URL for rotation pdf. :white_check_mark:
